**Differentiable Programming to Engineer Complex Systems.**

## About Me

I am a <span style="color: #0B2545;">**Quantitative Researcher at Glencore**</span> in Houston, where I build forecasting, optimization, and valuation models for North American natural gas and power markets. My work spans demand and supply forecasting across balancing authorities, LP-based storage dispatch and valuation, and walk-forward backtesting infrastructure for systematic trading strategies.

I recently completed my <span style="color: #B31B1B;">**Ph.D. in Systems Engineering at Cornell University**</span> (Applied Mathematics minor), where I was a member of the **Symbiotic Engineering and Analysis (SEA) Lab**. My dissertation developed differentiable simulation and gradient-based methods for the multidisciplinary design optimization of novel offshore systems. Before Cornell, I earned my B.S. in **Mathematics and Data Science** from Winona State University, Minnesota.

:::{.callout-note icon=false style="margin-top: 25px;"}
### 💼 What I'm Working On
At Glencore, I focus on **price forecasting, statistical arbitrage, and storage optimization** in natural gas markets — combining time-series models, supervised ML, convex optimization, and large-scale fundamental data pipelines to inform discretionary and systematic trading.

## Research & Applied Interests

I apply computational methods to design and operate large-scale systems — from offshore renewables to wholesale energy markets. My interests sit at the intersection of **optimization**, **machine learning**, and **physical/economic simulation**. In academia, I focused on **multidisciplinary design optimization (MDO)**, **control co-design**, and **differentiable programming** for complex engineered systems. In industry, I bring those same tools to **commodity trading research**: forecasting, valuation of physical assets (storage, generation), and systematic strategy development in natural gas and power markets.

![Research Interests](files/my%20reseach%20interests.png){.img-fluid style="width: 100%; max-width: 1200px; height: auto; display: block; margin: 20px auto;"}

Keywords: Time-Series Forecasting, Convex & Stochastic Optimization, Optimal Control, Differentiable Programming, Reinforcement Learning, System Architecture, Numerical Simulation (BEM, FDM, FEM), Data Science, Data Engineering, Energy & Commodity Markets.
